channel.title: World Stock News | Real-Time Stock Market News & Financial Intelligence
channel.description: Institutional-grade stock market coverage, Wall Street analysis, real-time macroeconomic reports, and cryptocurrency intelligence.

item.title: ‘Super’ El Niño may soon make your coffee super expensive
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: Agricultural markets around the world are already dealing with record-high diesel prices and high fertilizer costs. A “super” El Niño is almost guaranteed to make matters worse for farmers and consumers.

item.title: Medicare is a bargain. What America can’t afford is private health insurance.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Vance
item.description: Private insurance costs way more for the same results — or worse.

item.title: Polymarket traders see a 10% chance the AI bubble bursts before New Year’s Day
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Mehta
item.description: For investors worried that the runaway artificial-intelligence trade might be about to hit the skids, prediction markets are already starting to reflect that anxiety.

item.title: Elon Musk promised a SpaceX share to every kid in America — don’t hold your breath
item.dc:creator: Claire Montclaire
item.description: Trick or treat? Musk has a long record of saying things have little relation to reality.

item.title: AI stocks are probably in a bubble — but might be worth holding on to, says Citadel’s Ken Griffin
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: Investors are for sure facing “bubbles,” but Ken Griffin isn’t telling investors to dump those stocks.

item.title: Moderna is about to release the trial results for its cancer vaccine. A lot is riding on this data.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Vance
item.description: Moderna is one of the hottest stocks of the year because of its custom cancer treatment. Full Phase 3 data are set to be revealed this weekend.

item.title: Money-saving habits to cope with higher prices — from our readers
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Mehta
item.description: I asked people what they’re doing to make life more affordable today. I’ll definitely be trying some of these.

item.title: I receive 10 calls a day promising me $15,000 loans at 8% interest. Are these legitimate offers?
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: “They insist that the details will be provided after they have carried out a soft credit check.”

item.title: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
item.dc:creator: Marcus Vance
item.description: Wall Street’s Big Three have generated $52 billion in equity trading revenue this year, capturing about 80% of the market on rising margin lending to hedge funds.

item.title: Anthropic is AI trade's last big hope for a major IPO this year
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: On Kalshi, Anthropic is seen as the last major IPO in 2026 after OpenAI delayed its public market debut. Others have postponed too.

item.title: In the battle for AI supremacy, China is only six months behind the U.S — but that means it’s winning, says former Google CEO
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: AI is not a bubble, says Google’s former CEO. It’s real growth, real money, real customers paying for something useful.

item.title: We have a $300,000 mortgage with a 2.75% interest rate. I want to pay it off. My husband says I’m crazy. Who’s right?
item.dc:creator: Marcus Vance
item.description: “I don’t want to enter retirement owing six figures when we have the cash to clear it.”

item.title: George Foreman’s lavish Texas estate with 50-car garage is listed for $6 million
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Mehta
item.description: The sprawling Texas estate where boxing legend George Foreman spent the final decades of his life has hit the market for $6 million—offering a rare glimpse inside the private world of the heavyweight champion.

item.title: My sister moved in with our mother, 78, and says she deserves the $925,000 family home. Is she right?
item.dc:creator: Claire Montclaire
item.description: “The house is worth $925,000 and mom owns it outright. She also has $480,000 in investments.”

item.title: Robot factories and hypersonic missiles: JPMorgan Chase's first $5 billion of defense investments
item.dc:creator: Elena Rostova
item.description: With $5 billion already deployed off its balance sheet, JPMorgan Chase is racing ahead on direct investments in defense tech, hardware and supply chains.
